hints.title: Transitive Divisibility by Sorting
hints.text: Sorting the elements ensures that if nums[i] is divisible by nums[j], it is automatically divisible by all predecessors of nums[j].

hints.title: Longest Divisible Chain Recurrence
hints.text: Let dp[i] be the size of the largest divisible subset ending with nums[i]. Check all j less than i where nums[i] % nums[j] is zero.

hints.title: Parent Reconstruction Traceback
hints.text: Maintain parent pointers alongside dp values. When dp[j] plus one exceeds dp[i], update dp[i] and point parent[i] to j. Trace backward from the max element to assemble the subset.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N^2) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all powerset subsets takes exponential O(2^N) time, which overflows for N up to 1000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting plus 1D dynamic programming records predecessor pointers in O(N) space, finding the chain in O(N^2) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize the parallel with Longest Increasing Subsequence and reconstruct the subset via parent backtracking.
